newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel falls sharply against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel falls sharply against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed sharply lower against the dollar on Monday following intervention by the Bank of Israel, dealers said.

"The routine continues. The Bank of Israel had to intervene several times in the market to buy dollars after the basket fell by more than seven percent below the diagonal rate," said Guy Levi of Bank Leumi.
"The market was very quiet today and the central bank was the only major player," he said.
Traders estimated the central bank bought $100 million.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3510 shekels against 3.3410 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6368 shekels against 3.6349 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.6983 shekels per 100 yen against 2.6938 on Friday and against the mark at 1.9776 shekels against 1.9866 on Friday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3480 shekels.
